text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, traders said.

Jet prices remained weak with very little buying interest and good supplies in NWE blocking arbitrage. Egyptian, Italian and Libyan cargoes were seen available. Traders said July term contract pricing strategies were also keeping prices pegged down.

Gas oil prices remained fairly weak due to thin local demand but traders said some cargoes were still being mopped up by buying for a recent Indian tender while a $10-$13 arbitrage window to NWE was also providing a balance.
"Indian cargoes are still being covered in the Med but that should come to an end soon by today's economics," a trader said.
Traders said 0.2 sulphur cargoes were valued around $1 lower at $157 a tonne with diesel taking a $4 premium to this level.
Naphtha prices ended steady tracking a flat NWE market. Cargoes were notionally unchanged at $177/$179 cif.
No deals were heard done but mirrored activity in NWE where traders were watching the gasoline market for clues into demand for heavier naphthenic and aromatic material.
Gasoline cargoes were unchanged at a notional $196/$198 cif for premium unleaded.
High sulphur fuel oil cargoes were slightly stronger with some traders saying deals could be done around the $80 a tonne fob mark.
One cargo of 330 CST fuel oil was sold on Tuesday by a Spanish refiner at $83 a tonne fob, or the equivalent of $78.50 fob for 380 CST.
A second cargo of 330 centistoke high sulphur was reported traded at about $88 to $90 cif, or after factoring for quality, the equivalent of about $85 for 380 centistoke material.
But one trader was heard offering ISAB specification material which it could not find a home for in the Far East into the Mediterranean at $74.50 fob.
Low sulphur was reported to be a weak market with little demand. One trader said Israel has stopped buying material for power generation "which doesn't help matters".
Two cargoes on the water were being offered but sellers were not receiving any buying interest, a trader said.
